descriptor: Small-batch furniture, made to be repaired

voice.summary: Wren & Lodge writes the way a maker talks across a workbench: plainly, in the first person plural, with the occasional admission of a mistake. Sentences are long enough to breathe and short enough to be believed.
dos: Write in letter form, as 'we' speaking to 'you', and sign off with names
Give the real cost or the real flaw before the benefit
Use workshop nouns: oak, joint, glue, offcut, bench
donts: Never use words like premium, curated or bespoke
Do not hide a price or a delay behind soft phrasing
Avoid exclamation marks and sales urgency

taglines: Built to be mended, not replaced
A chair you can fix yourself
boilerplate: Wren & Lodge is a small furniture maker building repairable pieces from honest materials in limited batches, with fair pay and visible costs on every order.

microcopy.success: Thank you for reading. Write back any time.
microcopy.error: That did not go through. Please try once more.
microcopy.empty: Nothing here yet, but we are working on it.

logo.note: A simple house-and-roof shape reads as a workshop and a home, matching a furniture maker that speaks like a neighbour.
